Team A enters the grid in a 3v2 attack against Team B's two active defenders.

Team A uses Coerver group tactics?such as a central player using a Shimmy to hold the ball before slipping a pass to an overlapping winger?to score on goal.

Once the rep ends (goal, save, or out of bounds):

	The Team A attacker who took the shot/lost the ball immediately exits the pitch.
	The remaining 2 Team A players instantly become Defenders.
	Team C sends 3 new Attackers into the grid from the opposite end to attack Team A in a fresh 3v2.
Equipment: 1 Full-size goal (or 2 mini-goals at opposite ends) | 6 Cones (grid outlines and starting markers) | Multiple soccer balls
Coaching Points: Create Width & Depth: The two non-ball-carrying attackers must stretch the two defenders by staying wide, leaving the middle open for a 1v1 move or drive. | Drive at the Free Defender: The central player should dribble directly at one of the two defenders to isolate them into a 2v1 situation on the wing. | Immediate Transition: The moment possession changes, players must switch mental gears instantly from attack to defense.
Progressions: Level 1 (Must Use a Combination): A goal only counts if a wall pass, overlap, or takeover was executed during the build-up. | Level 2 (Trailing Defender): The 3rd defender for the defending team is allowed to sprint back into the play 3 seconds after the whistle, turning the 3v2 into a fast-recovering 3v3.
Notes:
Grid Size: 25 yards long $\times$ 20 yards wide (final third area).

Positions: Team A (3 Attackers) starts at midfield; Team B (2 Defenders) sets up inside the grid; 3rd Defender from Team B waits off the field; Team C waits off the sideline.

Coaching Focus: Develops 3-player attacking rotations, dynamic off
Purpose:
Team A attacks Team B in a 3v3 live scenario to score in Goal 1.

Team A utilizes 3-player combinations (e.g., central player performs a Double Scissors, passes wide, and makes a third-man overlap run).

If Team A scores or shoots wide, Team B leaves the pitch immediately.

Team C (waiting behind Goal 1) instantly passes a new ball in and attacks Team A toward Goal 2.

The game continues as an fast-paced "winner stays on" wave.
Equipment: 4 Corner Cones (grid boundary) | 2 Mini-goals (or full goals with goalkeepers) | Soccer balls stationed at both end lines
Coaching Points: Triangles of Support: Maintain an equilateral triangle shape when attacking so the ball carrier always has two distinct passing options (left/right or depth/width). | Third-Man Runs: When Player 1 passes to Player 2, Player 3 should already be sprinting into open space to receive the next touch from Player 2. | Speed of Combination: Keep touches light and quick; use Coerver footwork to create just enough space to deliver the combination pass.
Progressions: Level 1 (Third-Man Run Bonus): Goals count as double points if created via a third-man pass sequence. | Level 2 (Shot Clock): Attackers have 10 seconds total to get a shot off, forcing explosive forward combinations rather than passive possession.
Notes:
Grid Size: 30 yards long $\times$ 20 yards wide.

Positions: Team A and Team B play 3v3 inside the grid; Team C waits behind Goal 1, Team D waits behind Goal 2.

Coaching Focus: Trains tight-space group play using Coerver close-
Purpose:
Pair 1 starts with possession and can score in any of the 4 mini-goals.

Pair 1 is encouraged to use Coerver 2-player footwork combinations:

	Takeover: Ball carrier uses a Sole Roll or Shield, leaving the ball for their teammate running from the opposite direction.
	Give-and-Go: Quick one-touch return pass around an aggressive defender.

Pair 2 defends live to win possession and counter-attack into any of the 4 goals.

Play 90-second high-intensity shifts, then rotate pairs.
Equipment: 4 Cones (tight outer box) | 4 Mini-goals (one on each side of the box) | Multiple soccer balls
Coaching Points: Communication & Cueing: The player initiating the Takeover must shield the ball from the defender and leave it dead, while the runner calls for it clearly. | Deceptive Movement: Move away from your teammate first to drag your defender away, then cut back sharply to receive the pass or complete the crossover. | Spatial Awareness: With 4 targets, look to quickly switch the point of attack to an open goal whenever one side gets congested.
Progressions: Level 1 (Takeover Mandatory): Before a goal can be scored, the attacking pair must execute at least one clean Takeover hand-off. | Level 2 (One-Touch Finish): Shots on the mini-goals must be taken first-time off a combination pass.
Notes:
Grid Size: 15 yards $\times$ 15 yards square.

Goals: 4 mini-goals placed in the center of each of the 4 boundary lines.

Positions: Pair 1 (Attackers) vs. Pair 2 (Defenders) inside the box.
